key_insight: VERID is a persistent semantic digital twin that connects AI agents’ experimental plans to laboratory execution and supports iterative in-silico self-play.
engineering_relevance: A queryable, stateful laboratory model can help automation systems validate protocols, recover from execution errors, and preserve traceable experimental records.
method: Expose laboratory state through queryable semantic introspection.
Validate protocols with time-compressed simulation using discrete accounting.
Persist multimodal execution traces and provide a framework for safe execution.
evidence_signal: Three case studies using aqueous dye and deionized water mixtures demonstrate pre-emptive protocol-error detection, stateful mid-run recovery, and post-hoc identification of subtle physical failures.
watch_item: Validation is limited to dye-and-water studies; transfer to complex biochemical workflows and broader physical variability remains unestablished.
paper_title: Semantic Representation for Agentic Self-Play in Automated Laboratories
